name: THE AIRPORT TERMINAL
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 453, 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428 (roofs and cover); ask row 468's list, the eighth: 'THE AIRPORT TERMINAL: the long concourse, the gates, the baggage hall.'
facts: The valley's airport sits beside the Strip and moved tens of millions of passengers a year; a terminal is a ticketing hall, one checkpoint line everybody is squeezed through, a long concourse of gates behind a wall of glass, and a baggage hall below.

A CHECKPOINT IS BUILT TO BE A CHOKE: a line of scanners with lanes one person wide between them. In a fight that is the board: the floor's only ways across are the lanes, and the upper walkway over them.
When flights stop, a terminal fills with people who cannot leave and luggage nobody collects (every grounding has shown it: cots at the gates, bags in heaps at the carousels).
The map's own kind 'terminal' (engine/bohemia_fight_kinds.js: the transport zone, a roof of two and three storeys) is where it is fought.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (terminal_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The terminal is the one map kind with a concourse and a baggage hall. The parking garage takes its own share there first (garage.json); of the rest, this share is fought inside the terminal, by the cell's own dice; the rest on the kerb outside.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words).

wall.effect: The terminal's wall: no way through.

floor.effect: The terminal's floor, and the lanes through the checkpoint: open floor, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.
floor.say: The terminal's floor: open, nothing to hide behind.

checkpoint.effect: A scanner and its screens in the checkpoint's line: no way through, no sight through. The lanes between them are the only way across on the floor, and the only way a shot gets across.

counter.effect: A check-in counter or a gate's desk: low cover.

queue.effect: The queue's rails, still set out in their maze: slow going (3 AP a step) and low cover.
queue.say: The queue's rails: slow going, low cover.

luggage.effect: Suitcases nobody came back for, stacked into a wall: cover.

trolleys.effect: Luggage trolleys jammed together: low cover.

seats.effect: A gate's rows of seats, bolted down: slow going (3 AP a step) and low cover.
seats.say: Gate seats: slow going, low cover.

newsstand.effect: A newsstand, its shutter torn off: cover.

camp.effect: Somebody who never got a flight out lives here: bedding and bags. Low cover.

belt.effect: A baggage carousel's belt: you climb over it, slow going (3 AP a step), and it is low cover.
belt.say: The carousel's belt: slow going, low cover.

carousel.effect: The middle of a carousel, heaped with bags that came round and round: nobody stands on its tile; cover for the tiles beside it.

column.effect: A column: nobody stands on its tile.

fire.effect: A fire in a drum somebody keeps. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A drum fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The doors to the kerb, the glass gone: open floor, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The kerb's doors: open floor, and the day is on you.

high.effect: The upper walkway, half a storey up: high ground, nobody's at the bell, and at the checkpoint it is the one way across that is not a lane. A blow or a shot down from it lands easier, one up at it harder; a gun reaches a tile farther from it. Up the stairs it is a walk; over its rail from the floor it is a climb: no attack that turn, and a beast cannot.
high.say: The upper walkway: you hit down easier, and a gun reaches a tile more.

high_seats.effect: Seats on the upper walkway: low cover, on high ground.
high_seats.say: Seats on the walkway: low cover, and high ground.

high_luggage.effect: Luggage stacked on the upper walkway: cover, on high ground. The best ground in the terminal.
high_luggage.say: Luggage on the walkway: cover, and high ground.

ramp.effect: The stairs: the WALK up to the upper walkway. A step onto them from the floor costs one more; a man who walks up can still strike this turn.
ramp.say_before: The stairs: the walk up, and you can still strike.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK FIVE's own picture for it is in terminal_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL, RAIL, HEIGHT); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile. A DRESS piece is drawn and never counted.
open_sides_why: THE WALL OF GLASS: the terminal's long north side faces the apron and is glass from floor to roof, so by day the light falls along the whole of it and a man there is seen; at night it is as dark as anywhere.

say.height: The upper walkway: you hit down easier, and a gun reaches a tile more.

start_why: NOBODY HOLDS THE UPPER WALKWAY AT THE BELL: both lines start on the floor; the walkway is whoever takes the stairs first.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the terminal's long white roof, its ribs, its strips of skylight and its dead hanging signs over the board at this alpha (10%, never past the fight's own most). 'src' is the picture COOK FIVE makes (see garage.json's ceiling); 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in.
